body.statement: For every admissible compact family \(\mathcal K\), does ordinary differentiation of the all-active recursion along ambient empirical-process directions yield, uniformly over \(Q\in\mathcal K\), \[\sqrt N\{[M_N]_Q-[M_T]_Q\}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N[I_T(\xi_i)]_Q+o_{P_{N,Q}}(1),\] jointly with \(\sqrt N([\widehat P_{0X}]_Q-P_{0X,Q})\) on \(\mathcal F_{0X,T}\), while every row-averaged Taylor remainder for messages, Gram products, mean-score coordinates, and variance-score coordinates is \(o_{P_{N,Q}}(N^{-1/2})\) on \(\{\mathbb P_{N,Q}\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\}\)?
body.justification: This is the genuine proof boundary on a full-rank open neighborhood; no central limit theorem is assumed.
body.gap: First-order state evolution, concentration, and entrywise leave-one-out theory do not establish this aggregate root-\(N\) expansion for a reused-matrix causal recursion.
body.consumer: A positive answer yields analytic inference for every fixed-dimensional smooth Causal-MP moment configuration.
